{"ticker":"BHP","period":"FY26","period_type":"full_year","currency":"USD","metrics":{"revenue":{"value":"US$58.8bn","change_pct":"+15%","basis":"reported"},"underlying_npat":{"value":"US$13.2bn","change_pct":"+30%","basis":"underlying"},"underlying_eps":{"value":"260.0 US cps","change_pct":"+30%","basis":"underlying"},"dividend_ordinary":{"value":"US$0.99 per share","change_pct":"n/a","note":"Final dividend only; full-year total US$1.72 per share fully franked; H1 FY26 interim was US$0.73 per share; no special dividend declared"},"operating_cash_flow":{"value":"US$21.8bn","change_pct":"+17%","basis":"reported"}},"summary":"BHP delivered a strong beat on underlying earnings, with Underlying EBITDA of US$32.9bn (+27%) and Underlying attributable profit of US$13.2bn (+30%), driven overwhelmingly by a 35% surge in copper realised prices to US$5.74/lb that more than offset a 3% volume decline. Cash conversion was exceptional: US$21.8bn operating cash flow yielded US$9.8bn free cash flow (+83%), and net debt collapsed from US$12.9bn to US$8.7bn, aided materially by the US$4.3bn Antamina silver streaming proceeds. The US$0.99 final dividend (fully franked, 72% payout ratio) brings the full-year return to US$1.72 per share, the highest in four years, signalling management confidence in the balance sheet and copper outlook. The primary forward risk is a copper price correction: at spot, the portfolio generates ~US$50bn in five-year cumulative FCF, but the Jansen Stage 2 cost blowout (US$4.9bn to US$6.9bn) and a US$2.3bn impairment are an early warning that the potash mega-project carries meaningful execution risk as capital spending accelerates to ~US$11bn pa through FY31.","full_analysis":"## Executive summary
- **Copper is now the majority earnings engine**: Copper segment contributed 54% of Group Underlying EBITDA (US$18.2bn, +48%) for the first time, driven by a 35% lift in realised copper prices to US$5.74/lb; this is structurally the most important shift in BHP's earnings mix in a decade.
- **Price was the overwhelming driver, not volume**: Revenue rose US$7.5bn but copper volumes fell 3% (grade decline at Escondida) and iron ore volumes were flat; 86% of the EBITDA uplift came from external price factors (US$7.3bn net price impact vs US$1.3bn controllable/operational uplift).
- **Jansen Stage 2 cost blowout and impairment are a red flag**: JS2 capex was revised from US$4.9bn to US$6.9bn (+41%), triggering a US$2.3bn impairment charge (statutory profit US$9.8bn vs underlying US$13.2bn; the US$3.4bn gap after tax is the largest exceptional drag in years).
- **Balance sheet deleveraged sharply but partly via asset monetisation**: Net debt fell from US$12.9bn to US$8.7bn, but US$4.3bn of that came from the Antamina silver streaming transaction — an accounting event, not operating performance.
- **Samarco tail liability remains material**: Provision stands at US$5.2bn (30 June 2026); UK group action second-stage trial scheduled April 2027–March 2028; FY27 and FY28 cash outflows (BHP share) are US$0.9bn and US$0.5bn respectively.

## Key numbers

| Metric | FY26 | FY25 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | US$58.8bn | US$51.3bn | +15% |
| Underlying EBITDA | US$32.9bn | US$26.0bn | +27% |
| Underlying EBITDA margin | 59% | 53% | +6pp |
| Statutory (attributable) NPAT | US$9.8bn | US$9.0bn | +9% |
| Underlying attributable NPAT | US$13.2bn | US$10.2bn | +30% |
| Exceptional items (after tax) | -US$3.4bn | -US$1.2bn | worsened |
| Basic EPS (statutory) | 193.6 US cps | 177.8 US cps | +9% |
| Underlying EPS | 260.0 US cps | 200.2 US cps | +30% |
| Net operating cash flow | US$21.8bn | US$18.7bn | +17% |
| Capex & exploration | US$10.3bn | US$9.8bn | +5% |
| Free cash flow | US$9.8bn | US$5.3bn | +83% |
| Net debt | US$8.7bn | US$12.9bn | -33% |
| Net debt / Underlying EBITDA | 0.3x | ~0.5x | improved |
| Gearing ratio | 13.4% | 19.8% | improved |
| Underlying ROCE | 26.1% | 20.6% | +5.5pp |

**Bridge: statutory to underlying NPAT** — Exceptional items of -US$2.771bn (pre-tax) included: US$2.3bn Jansen impairment + US$1.1bn Samarco dam failure charge, partially offset by other items. After-tax impact approximately -US$3.4bn.

## Quality of earnings
- **Cash conversion is high**: Operating cash flow of US$21.8bn on Underlying EBITDA of US$32.9bn implies a cash conversion ratio of ~66% (consistent with a heavily capital-intensive business and US$2.0bn Samarco settlement payments). Free cash flow of US$9.8bn is clean and well above the prior year.
- **Silver streaming proceeds inflate apparent deleveraging**: The US$4.3bn Antamina silver streaming transaction is classified as portfolio management cash flow, helping cut net debt to US$8.7bn. Investors should note that this monetises future silver royalty revenue (a recurring earnings headwind going forward), and is not repeated operational free cash flow.
- **No significant receivables or inventory concerns disclosed**: Positive inventory timing movements at Escondida and BMA contributed to controllable cost improvements; these are acknowledged as one-off timing items in the EBITDA waterfall and could reverse.
- **Copper SA unit cost of US$0.32/lb**: The 73% reduction was driven by exceptionally high gold, silver, and uranium by-product credits at gold prices well above guidance assumptions (gold was US$4,300/oz in guidance; spot averaged materially higher). At normalised by-product prices, unit costs would be structurally higher — the by-product windfall is real but price-dependent.
- **Adjusted effective tax rate 36.5%** (FY25: 37.2%); including royalties 42.9% — BHP's true government take is substantial and a source of recurring earnings drag.

## Management framing
**Rating: Mixed — mostly transparent, selectively promotional**
- **Transparent**: BHP clearly disclosed the Jansen Stage 2 cost blowout (+41%), the associated US$2.3bn impairment, and the Samarco provision. The EBITDA waterfall honestly attributes ~81% of earnings improvement to price (external) vs only ~19% to controllable/operational factors.
- **Promotional**: The headline narrative — "majority of earnings from copper", "record" copper EBITDA, "self-funding" growth — is technically accurate but buries the fact that copper volumes actually fell 3% and that the price tailwind (copper +35% realised) did all the heavy lifting. The emphasis on "6% unit cost reduction" across major assets mixes genuine BOS-driven savings with the exceptional Copper SA by-product windfall.
- **Omitted / downplayed**: The silver streaming monetisation (US$4.3bn) is presented as a capital-unlocking initiative without foregrounding that it permanently reduces future silver earnings from Antamina. The Escondida New Concentrator capex range has been revised upward (US$4.4–5.9bn to US$5.4–6.3bn), quietly noted in the operations section but not prominently flagged as a cost escalation.
- **Copper SA unit costs**: Management celebrates US$0.32/lb unit costs, but the guidance for FY27 is US$0.30–0.80/lb — an enormous range that reflects the price sensitivity of gold/uranium by-product offsets. The FY26 outcome at the lower end of this range required gold at record prices.

## Segments

| Segment | Revenue | Underlying EBITDA | EBITDA margin | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Copper (statutory) | US$29.0bn | US$18.2bn | 70% | +48% EBITDA |
| — Escondida | US$17.1bn | US$12.4bn | ~73% | +45% |
| — Pampa Norte (Spence) | US$2.9bn | US$1.6bn | ~56% | +23% |
| — Copper SA | US$6.0bn | US$3.2bn | ~53% | +65% |
| Iron Ore (statutory) | US$23.9bn | US$14.5bn | 61% | +1% |
| — WAIO | US$23.7bn | US$14.7bn | 62% | +2% |
| Coal (statutory) | US$5.6bn | US$0.83bn | 15% | +45% |
| — BMA | US$3.9bn | US$0.70bn | 18% | +19% |
| — NSWEC | US$1.9bn | US$0.23bn | 12% | +48% |
| Group & Unallocated | n/a | -US$0.60bn | n/a | improved |

**Key drivers**:
- Copper: realised price +35% was the entire story; Escondida volumes fell 3% on planned grade decline (feed grade fell from 1.02% to 0.90%).
- Iron ore: volumes flat (record WAIO shipments 291Mt, 100% basis), price +3%; Middle East conflict drove diesel costs up ~30%, adding US$316m headwind; margin flat at 61%.
- Coal: BMA EBITDA +19% on higher steelmaking coal price (+8%) and highest stripping volumes in five years. NSWEC +48% on higher bypass coal volumes. Coal is only 3% of Group EBITDA — immaterial.
- Potash (development): US$326m EBITDA loss (capex burn); Jansen Stage 1 84% complete, on track for mid-CY27.

## Balance sheet
- Net debt fell from US$12.9bn to US$8.7bn (gearing 13.4%, well below the US$10–20bn target range).
- The decline was driven by: US$9.8bn free cash flow + US$4.3bn silver streaming proceeds + US$0.8bn asset sales — less US$6.8bn dividends to shareholders and US$2.4bn to NCIs and US$2.0bn Samarco obligations.
- **Debt maturity profile is well-spread**: No near-term refinancing cliff; maturities concentrated FY32–FY42; 89% capital markets, A1/A rated.
- Post-dividend (pro-forma), net debt moves back toward ~US$13.7bn (paying US$5.0bn final), re-entering the target range at the lower end.
- Samarco provision: US$5.2bn (FY25: US$5.8bn). UK litigation second-stage trial April 2027–March 2028 is an unquantified contingent liability.
- WA Nickel (Nickel West + West Musgrave) in care and maintenance; net operating assets -US$297m (provision-heavy). No impairment in FY26 but this remains a stranded asset risk.

## Dividend and capital allocation
- Final dividend: US$0.99 per share (fully franked), total FY26 dividends US$1.72 per share (US$8.7bn), the highest in four years.
- Payout ratio: 66% of underlying attributable profit (72% on the final dividend basis as stated by BHP, calculated differently).
- Total shareholder returns since CAF inception (FY16): >US$115bn — a genuine track record.
- Capital and exploration expenditure of US$10.3bn in FY26; FY27 guidance ~US$11bn; expected to remain at ~US$11bn in FY28 and on average FY29–FY31, driven by Jansen Stage 2 cost escalation.
- Growth capex is predominantly copper-focused (>55% of ~US$4bn pa growth capex); management claims copper growth is self-funding at consensus prices — credible at current copper prices but price-sensitive.
- No buyback announced; no special dividend. Given net debt is below the target floor (pro-forma ~US$13.7bn after final dividend), there is limited scope for additional near-term returns absent further asset monetisations.

## Guidance and outlook
- **FY27 copper production guidance**: 1,650–1,800 kt (vs 1,953 kt in FY26, a -10% to -15% decline) — Escondida guidance 1,000–1,100 kt vs 1,261 kt in FY26, reflecting planned further grade decline to ~0.70%.
- **FY27 WAIO production**: 253–264 Mt (100% basis: 286–298 Mt); unit costs US$20.25–21.75/t (vs US$19.66/t in FY26) — diesel exposure is the swing factor (US$10/bbl = ~US$0.15/t).
- **Medium-term targets**: WAIO >305 Mtpa from Q4 FY28; WAIO unit costs <US$19/t in FY29; BMA 43–45 Mtpa at <US$120/t medium-term.
- **Capex**: ~US$11bn FY27; same FY28 and FY29–31 average (Jansen Stage 2 escalation absorbed).
- **Adjusted effective tax rate FY27**: 35–40%.
- **No revenue or NPAT guidance provided** (standard for BHP).
- **Vicuña Stage I FID**: Potential as early as end of CY26 — significant incremental capital commitment.
- **Escondida New Concentrator FID**: CY27–28; first production CY31–32; capex US$5.4–6.3bn (BHP share).

## Positives
- **Record copper EBITDA of US$18.2bn (+48%)**: Copper at 70% EBITDA margin is extraordinary; Escondida's US$12.4bn EBITDA is one of the highest-margin mining assets globally.
- **Free cash flow +83% to US$9.8bn**: Strong, clean cash generation post-capex; balance sheet now at 0.3x net debt/EBITDA.
- **Group unit costs -6.1%**: Real cost discipline in an inflationary environment (4% Australia, 3.7% Chile); WAIO achieved real unit cost decline for the 7th consecutive year.
- **Record WAIO production (291 Mt, 100% basis)**: Operational reliability at the world's lowest-cost major iron ore operation.
- **FY26 total dividend US$1.72/share fully franked**: Highest in four years; signals balance sheet confidence.
- **Copper SA unit costs -73% to US$0.32/lb**: Record EBITDA of US$3.2bn and ~US$1.0bn FCF from this asset demonstrates Olympic Dam / Carrapateena system generating real cash.
- **Jansen Stage 1 on track**: 84% complete, first production mid-CY27; potash adds portfolio diversification.
- **BOS driving ~US$5bn cumulative cost savings since FY20**: Quantified and verifiable productivity

{
  "ticker": "CSL",
  "period": "FY26",
  "period_type": "full_year",
  "currency": "USD",
  "metrics": {
    "revenue":             {"value": "US$15,797m", "change_pct": "+2%", "basis": "reported"},
    "underlying_npat":     {"value": "US$2,837m",  "change_pct": "-3%", "basis": "underlying"},
    "underlying_eps":      {"value": "US$6.43",    "change_pct": "-3%", "basis": "underlying"},
    "dividend_ordinary":   {"value": "US$2.92",    "change_pct": "0%",  "note": "maintained flat vs FY25; franking not disclosed in this presentation"},
    "operating_cash_flow": {"value": "US$3,512m",  "change_pct": "-1%", "basis": "reported"}
  },
  "summary": "FY26 delivered results consistent with CSL's own May 2026 guidance update, so no surprise vs management expectations, though the underlying NPAT of US$2,837m fell -3% on a reported basis and -3% at constant currency — a deceleration from the prior growth trajectory. The primary drag was CSL Vifor: alumin price collapse in China (-17%), iron generic competition (-16% in iron), and the TAVNEOS marketing authorisation revocation combined to overwhelm Behring's modest Ig stability and Seqirus's +4% seasonal influenza growth. Cash conversion is solid — operating cash flow of US$3,512m is 124% of underlying NPAT, but the headline statutory result is a US$2,579m net loss driven by US$7.1b in non-cash impairments (US$4.9b in CSL Vifor intangibles/goodwill alone), confirming the Vifor acquisition destroyed substantial value. The dividend is held flat at US$2.92 per share, a signal of financial caution rather than confidence, accompanied by a completed A$1b buyback and a committed A$1.1b FY27 buyback. The single biggest forward risk is the structural deterioration of CSL Vifor — with a guided ~25% revenue decline in FY27, further anticipated impairments of ~US$200m, and TDAPA expiry for VELPHORO on 31 December 2026, the acquired nephrology/iron franchise is becoming a material earnings drag rather than the growth driver originally promised.",
  "full_analysis": "## Executive Summary
- FY26 was explicitly labelled a 'reset year' by management; an interim CEO was installed mid-year to drive a restructuring/transformation program, signalling the prior strategy failed to deliver.
- Underlying NPAT fell -3% (reported, -3% at CC) to US$2,837m on revenue up +2% reported but -1% at constant currency — FX tail-wind masked operational weakness.
- A US$7.1b pre-tax impairment charge (US$6.0b post-tax net of NCI) turned a ~US$3b underlying profit into a US$2,579m statutory net loss; US$4.9b of impairments relate directly to CSL Vifor goodwill and intangibles, a damning verdict on the ~US$11.7b acquisition.
- **Red flag:** CSL Vifor is guided to decline ~25% in revenue in FY27 with further ~US$200m impairments anticipated; the segment is structurally impaired, not cyclically weak.
- Cost-out program delivered US$176m of savings in FY26 (above target), rising to US$400m in FY27 and up to US$550m by FY28 — this is the primary near-term earnings lever.

## Key Numbers

| Metric | FY26 | FY25 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total Revenue | US$15,797m | US$15,558m | +2% reported; -1% CC |
| Gross Profit (underlying) | US$8,454m | US$8,443m | flat |
| Gross Margin % (underlying) | 53.5% | 54.3% | -80bps |
| Operating Result (underlying) | US$6,763m | US$6,827m | -1% |
| R&D (underlying) | US$1,223m | US$1,359m | -10% |
| G&A (underlying) | US$920m | US$1,000m | -8% |
| NPATA (underlying, to CSL shareholders) | US$3,098m | US$3,219m | -4% |
| Underlying NPAT (to CSL shareholders) | US$2,837m | US$2,972m | -5% |
| Statutory NPAT (Loss) | -US$2,579m | +US$3,002m | n/m |
| Underlying NPATA EPS | US$6.43 | US$6.65 | -3% |
| Operating Cash Flow | US$3,512m | US$3,561m | -1% |
| Capex | US$766m | n/a (est. ~US$700m from chart) | n/a |
| Free Cash Flow (approx.) | ~US$2,746m | n/a | n/a |
| Net Debt | ~US$9.4b (chart) | ~US$9.3b (chart) | flat |
| Net Debt/EBITDA | 1.8x | 1.8x | flat |

Note: Statutory NPAT bridge: Underlying NPAT US$2,837m less restructuring/impairment post-tax US$6,000m plus NCI share of impairment US$584m = statutory loss US$2,579m.

## Quality of Earnings
- **Cash conversion is strong:** Operating cash flow of US$3,512m vs underlying NPAT of US$2,837m implies a cash conversion ratio of ~124%, reflecting non-cash amortisation and working capital discipline. This is genuine.
- **One-offs are large and real:** US$7.1b pre-tax impairment is non-cash but represents genuine economic value destruction on the Vifor acquisition. The US$799m cash restructuring charge (US$339m paid in FY26, ~US$300m to be paid in FY27) is a real cash cost that will weigh on FCF in FY27.
- **R&D cut is a double-edged sword:** R&D declined 13% at CC to US$1,223m. While marketed as 'disciplined reinvestment,' sustained R&D cuts in a biologics company risk medium-term pipeline erosion; management is partly offsetting this via the VMX-C001 (~US$50m) and clazakizumab programmes.
- **Tax rate deterioration:** Underlying NPATA ETR rose from 15.9% in FY25 to 20.8% in FY26 (FY25 benefited from favourable FX on deferred tax); this alone suppressed underlying NPAT growth by approximately US$150m.
- **FX was a net revenue tailwind:** Reported revenue was US$15,797m vs US$15,371m at CC, implying FX added US$426m to revenue but reduced underlying NPAT by a net ~US$44m (translation drag on profit).

## Management Framing
**Rating: Mixed — selectively transparent but promotional in emphasis.**
- Management led with 'consistent with May 2026 update' to frame the result as expected — true, but this was itself a downgrade event. The framing deflects from the fact that FY26 underlying NPAT is -3% on a base that was already below long-term targets.
- The US$7.1b impairment and statutory US$2,579m loss are disclosed clearly in the financials table, which is credit; however the deck's visual hierarchy strongly emphasises 'Underlying NPATA' and 'transformation progress,' ensuring the statutory loss does not dominate the narrative.
- **Omissions:** No per-segment underlying EBIT or NPAT is given — only 'Operating Result' (pre-R&D, pre-G&A). CSL Vifor's true profitability contribution post-R&D and interest allocation is not transparent.
- The US$176m cost save is highlighted as 'above target' but the target was not disclosed, making 'above target' unverifiable.
- The clazakizumab Eli Lilly deal ($100m upfront) is buried in the Behring operational slides — this is a meaningful revenue item for FY26 'Other Revenue' (+32% at Behring) and the deck should have called it out at the group level.
- FY27 guidance for Vifor at -25% revenue is to management's credit — this is blunt and rare for a company in transformation mode.

## Segments

| Segment | FY26 Revenue | Change (CC) | Operating Result | Op. Margin | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CSL Behring | US$11,387m | -1% | US$4,612m | 40.5% | -140bps |
| CSL Vifor | US$2,379m | +3% | US$1,252m | 52.6% | +370bps |
| CSL Seqirus | US$2,031m | -8% | US$899m | 44.3% | -230bps |

**CSL Behring (-1% CC):** Ig revenue (US$6,248m) was flat — Medicare Part D weighed on 1H, 2H recovered +7% on PCP. Albumin was the biggest drag at -17% (US$1,115m) on Chinese government price controls. ANDEMBRY (HAE) launched strongly (+14% HAE therapy group to US$884m) and HEMGENIX grew 25% to US$118m from a small base. KCENTRA ongoing price erosion (-17%) is a persistent headache. Operating margin contracted 140bps to 40.5% on gross margin decline (-70bps) and higher S&M spend (+8%).

**CSL Vifor (+3% CC):** The +3% and +370bps margin expansion look superficially good but are entirely driven by VELPHORO TDAPA inclusion (Nephrology Dialysis +18% to US$1,036m) — a regulatory temporary add-on payment that expires 31 December 2026, creating a significant cliff. Iron revenue fell -16% (US$915m) on generic competition. TAVNEOS had its marketing authorisation revoked. The segment margin expansion is TDAPA-distorted and will reverse sharply in FY27.

**CSL Seqirus (-8% CC):** Seasonal influenza grew +4% to US$1,578m on the back of adjuvanted (FLUAD, +5%) and cell-based (FLUCELVAX, +5%) portfolios. Total revenue fell -8% due to non-recurring avian influenza revenue (~US$270m In-license/Other, -47%) that was present in FY25. Operating margin contracted 230bps to 44.3% as fixed costs and reinvestment outpaced core revenue growth.

## Balance Sheet
- Net debt ~US$9.4b (per chart), net debt/EBITDA at 1.8x (within target 1.5x-2.0x range), aided by exclusion of restructuring/impairment from EBITDA denominator.
- De-leveraging trajectory has stalled: leverage flat at 1.8x year-on-year despite strong operating cash flow, as buybacks (~A$1b = ~US$675m) and ongoing capex (US$766m) absorbed cash generation.
- FY27 capex guided at ~US$1b (+/-US$100m), a step-up driven by Kankakee Ig facility investment. Combined with ~US$300m restructuring cash outflow and A$1.1b buyback, FCF will be materially absorbed.
- Impairments have structurally reduced the asset base; CSL Vifor's remaining intangible/goodwill carrying value is materially lower post the US$4.9b write-down, reducing future impairment risk from Vifor but not eliminating it (~US$200m anticipated FY27).
- No covenant stress evident at 1.8x leverage; sufficient headroom.

## Dividend and Capital Allocation
- FY26 DPS maintained at US$2.92 (flat vs FY25), signalling the board prioritised stability over growth signalling.
- With a statutory net loss, the dividend is technically being paid from retained earnings/distributable reserves — not current year earnings. This is technically fine but worth noting.
- A$1b on-market buyback completed in FY26; A$1.1b buyback committed for FY27. At current AUD/USD (~0.67), FY27 buyback ~US$740m. Total capital return in FY27 (dividend + buyback) ~US$1.45b.
- Capital allocation question: committing to A$1.1b buyback while guiding to ~US$1b capex and absorbing US$300m restructuring cash costs limits M&A optionality in FY27.

## Guidance and Outlook
- **FY27 Revenue:** In-line with FY26 at constant currency (i.e. flat at ~US$15.4b CC). FX headwind of ~US$50m at current rates.
- **FY27 Underlying NPAT:** ~+5% growth at constant currency. Implies ~US$2,980m underlying NPAT at CC (vs US$2,837m reported FY26 / US$2,881m CC). Key drivers: (1) cost saves ramping to US$400m, (2) Behring mid-single digit revenue growth, (3) Seqirus low single digit growth, partially offset by (4) Vifor revenue -25% and (5) higher acquired IP amortisation (post-tax IP amortisation increases ~US$90m CSL share in FY27, a meaningful headwind to bridge from NPATA to NPAT).
- **Anticipated FY27 impairments:** ~US$200m (pre-tax, pre-NCI) — further Vifor-related charges.
- Guidance is quantified and reasonably specific — credit to management for this rather than vague directional language.

## Positives
- ANDEMBRY (HAE) launch exceeded expectations: US$240m in first full year across 19 markets; HAE therapy group +14% to US$884m.
- HEMGENIX (gene therapy for Haemophilia B) grew +25% to US$118m, validating the gene therapy strategy even at a modest scale.
- Cost-out program US$176m in FY26, above internal target, ramping to US$400m by FY27 — this is a real near-term earnings driver.
- Operating cash flow US$3,512m is 124% of underlying NPAT; cash quality is genuine and the balance sheet is not under stress.
- Seqirus seasonal influenza portfolio grew +4% despite a challenging US market and the loss of non-recurring avian flu revenue; differentiated portfolio (FLUAD, FLUCELVAX) gaining share.
- Net Debt/EBITDA at 1.8x within target range with meaningful buyback capacity retained.
- Clazakizumab licensing deal with Eli Lilly ($100m upfront) monetises pipeline and validates asset quality.
- Ig 2H recovery (+7% on PCP) confirms underlying demand is intact once channel inventory normalised and Medicare Part D headwinds absorbed.

## Negatives / Red Flags
- **Vifor acquisition destruction:** US$7.1b pre-tax impairment in a single year, predominantly CSL Vifor (US$4.9b of intangibles/goodwill). The ~US$11.7b acquisition is confirmed as value-destroying; cumulative Vifor impairments now dwarf any earnings contribution.
- **Vifor structural decline:** FY27 guided at -25% revenue (iron generics, VELPHORO TDAPA expiry Dec 2026, TAVNEOS revoked). The segment will shrink from US$2.4b to ~US$1.8b in one year.
- **Albumin China implosion:** -17% to US$1,115m on government cost containment; 2H was only down 5% suggesting some stabilisation, but this market has permanently reset lower and represents ~10% of Behring revenue.
- **Tax rate normalisation:** ETR rose from 15.9% to 20.8%; FY25 was artificially low. Higher normalised tax
